sources.title: Sobral G, Dubuc C, Winters S, Ruiz-Lambides A, Emery Thompson M, Maestripieri D, Milich KM. (2024). Facial and genital color ornamentation, testosterone, and reproductive output in high-ranking male rhesus macaques. Scientific Reports 14:2621.
sources.locator: Abstract; Methods, Study animals and offspring-paternity calculations; Results, Effect of androgen and color ornamentation on mating and reproductive output; Discussion.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the article.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Article copyright notice states open access under CC BY 4.0; Article also reports IACUC protocol A0100108.
sources.licenseAppliesTo: Article text; claims are paraphrased and no figures, tables, or supplementary files are reproduced.
sources.attribution: Sobral G, Dubuc C, Winters S, Ruiz-Lambides A, Emery Thompson M, Maestripieri D, Milich KM. (2024). Facial and genital color ornamentation, testosterone, and reproductive output in high-ranking male rhesus macaques. Scientific Reports 14:2621. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-52400-0. CC BY 4.0. Claims are paraphrased.
sources.scope: A study of 21 high-ranking adult male rhesus macaques aged 7–21 years in nine groups of the semi-free-ranging, food- and water-provisioned Cayo Santiago population, Puerto Rico; mating-season records were collected in February–July 2013. Reproductive success used paternity samples taken when offspring were yearlings, so infants dying before sampling were not assigned to sires. University of Puerto Rico Medical Sciences Campus IACUC protocol A0100108 is stated; no separate field permit is reported in the article.

gaps: The selected population-genomics study does not assess species-level anatomical morphology or its full variation.

The result is limited to high-ranking males, one provisioned island population, one mating season, and paternity records for offspring surviving to yearling sampling; it does not establish species-wide reproductive aging or lifetime fecundity.

claims.text: Among 21 high-ranking adult male rhesus macaques aged 7–21 years in nine groups at the provisioned, semi-free-ranging Cayo Santiago population, age predicted the number of offspring recorded for the 2013 mating-season study, with older males siring fewer offspring. Paternity sampling occurred at the yearling stage; infants that died before sampling were not assigned to sires, so the result is limited to offspring counted by the study protocol.
claims.textZh: 在波多黎各圣地亚哥岛一个有补饲的半自由活动群体中，研究了来自 9 个群体、年龄为 7–21 岁的 21 只高等级成年雄性恒河猴。年龄可预测 2013 年交配季研究记录的后代数量，年龄较大的雄性记录到的后代较少。亲子鉴定样本在幼体达到一岁时采集；采样前死亡的幼体无法归属父亲，因此结论仅适用于该研究流程记录到的后代。
claims.locator: Abstract; Methods, Study animals and offspring-paternity calculations; Results, Effect of androgen and color ornamentation on mating and reproductive output; Discussion.
claims.placeTimeScope: Cayo Santiago, Puerto Rico; 21 high-ranking adult males from nine social groups; behavioral and biological data for the 2013 mating season, February–July 2013.
claims.lifeStatus: Semi-free-ranging rhesus macaques in a managed island population provisioned with food and water; this is not an unprovisioned wild population or a species-wide demographic estimate.

claims.text: In one free-ranging troop of 64 rhesus macaques in the buffer zone of Buxa Tiger Reserve, West Bengal, India, observed from October 2013 to September 2014, fruit comprised 70.8% of the diet in the study-defined non-provisioning period (May–September) and 28.8% in the provisioning period (October–April). Mean daily range was 4.72 km and 2.58 km for those periods, respectively. These are seasonal observations of one troop and do not isolate provisioning from every seasonal influence or describe the species as a whole.
claims.textZh: 在印度西孟加拉邦布克萨虎保护区缓冲区一个由 64 只恒河猴组成的自由活动群体中，研究于 2013 年 10 月至 2014 年 9 月进行观察。按研究定义，5–9 月为无投喂期、10–4 月为投喂期；水果分别占这两个时期饮食的 70.8% 和 28.8%，平均日活动距离分别为 4.72 千米和 2.58 千米。这是对单一群体的季节性观察，无法排除所有季节影响，也不能代表整个物种。
claims.locator: Methods, Study Area and Study Troop; Results, Fruit availability, degree of provisioning and degree of frugivory and Sites of seed deposition; Table 3.
claims.placeTimeScope: Damanpur Block in the buffer zone of Buxa Tiger Reserve, West Bengal, India; one troop observed October 2013–September 2014. The article defines May–September as non-provisioning and October–April as provisioning.
claims.lifeStatus: One free-ranging troop exposed to seasonal tourist and local food provisioning; no captive animals were studied.

gaps: The study covers one troop and one annual cycle; broader populations, geographic variation, and causal effects independent of season remain unassessed.

claims.text: Liu et al. analyzed 81 geo-referenced wild Chinese rhesus macaques from five subspecies and 17 locations. Their population analyses resolved five genetic lineages across mainland China and Hainan and reported evidence of recent gene flow; these results describe the Chinese sample and study models.
claims.textZh: Liu 等人分析了来自中国 17 个地点、代表 5 个亚种的 81 只具有地理定位信息的野生恒河猴。群体分析识别出分布于中国大陆和海南的 5 个遗传谱系，并报告近期基因流动证据；这些结果限于该研究样本和模型。
claims.locator: Abstract; Results and Discussion, “Genetic diversity, phylogeny, and population structure”; Figure 1.
claims.placeTimeScope: Wild-born rhesus macaques sampled at 17 locations in China; the paper's population structure and gene-flow inferences are analysis-specific.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild-born animals; captive reference populations appear only as separately identified context.

gaps: The study samples Chinese populations and does not synthesize the species' complete evolutionary history, all subspecies, or all regions.

claims.text: The genomic survey included wild Chinese rhesus macaques from 17 locations on mainland China and Hainan. These sample locations document the study's geographic coverage and do not delimit the species' current global range.
claims.textZh: 该基因组调查纳入了中国大陆和海南 17 个地点的野生恒河猴。这些采样地点仅说明研究的地理覆盖范围，并未界定该物种当前的全球分布。
claims.locator: Abstract; Results and Discussion, “Genetic diversity, phylogeny, and population structure”; Figure 1 and Supplementary Table S1.
claims.placeTimeScope: Seventeen study locations in China; sampling describes the survey, not the full geographic distribution.

gaps: No complete current or historical range inventory was conducted.
The selected study does not review the fossil record.
No formal conservation assessment, global population trend, or risk category was reviewed.

reasons: One Cayo Santiago reproductive study supplements local Indian troop ecology and Chinese population-genomic evidence; morphology, fossil evidence, and conservation remain unassessed, while other supported facets remain partial.
No full life-history synthesis, systematic species-wide literature review, or independent expert review has been completed.

sources.title: Ram et al. (2015), Pre-Historic and Recent Vicariance Events Shape Genetic Structure and Diversity in Endangered Lion-Tailed Macaque in the Western Ghats: Implications for Conservation
sources.version: PLOS ONE 10(11): e0142597; version of record published 2015-11-11
sources.locator: Abstract; Methods, “Study area” and “Sample collection”; Results, “Genetic structure and diversity of lion-tailed macaques in the Western Ghats” and “Genetic diversity in the fragmented population of Anamalai hills”; Figures 1–2; Tables 1 and 3.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the article copyright notice.
sources.scope: Primary mitochondrial-DNA study of wild Western Ghats samples, with separately identified captive samples in some analyses. Claims are paraphrased and limited to sampled sites and markers; figures and sequences are not redistributed.
sources.rightsHolder: Muthuvarmadam S. Ram, Minal Marne, Ajay Gaur, Honnavalli N. Kumara, Mewa Singh, Ajith Kumar, Govindhaswamy Umapathy and coauthors as named in the article copyright notice.
sources.licenseAppliesTo: Article text under the stated CC BY 4.0 license; separately credited third-party material is excluded.
sources.attribution: Ram MS, Marne M, Gaur A, et al. (2015). Pre-Historic and Recent Vicariance Events Shape Genetic Structure and Diversity in Endangered Lion-Tailed Macaque in the Western Ghats: Implications for Conservation. PLoS ONE 10(11):e0142597. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0142597. Claims are paraphrased.

gaps: The mitochondrial-DNA study does not assess species-level anatomical morphology.
No life-cycle, reproductive, growth, survival, or longevity evidence was assessed.
The study does not provide a bounded assessment of diet or broader ecological interactions.

claims.text: Ram et al. recovered north-of-Palghat-gap and south-of-Palghat-gap mitochondrial clades among sampled lion-tailed macaques. A fossil-calibrated analysis of 893 mitochondrial bases estimated a mean time to their most recent common ancestor of 2.11 million years; this is a model-based estimate from mitochondrial markers, not a genome-wide species split date.
claims.textZh: Ram 等人在受采样的狮尾猕猴中识别出帕尔加特山口以北和以南的线粒体分支。基于 893 个线粒体碱基的化石校准分析，将其最近共同祖先的平均时间估为 211 万年前；这是线粒体标记的模型估计，不是全基因组物种分化日期。
claims.locator: Results, “Genetic structure and diversity of lion-tailed macaques in the Western Ghats”; Figure 4; Table 2.
claims.placeTimeScope: Sampled Macaca silenus populations north and south of the Palghat gap in the Western Ghats; divergence time is a fossil-calibrated mitochondrial-model estimate.
claims.lifeStatus: Primarily wild fecal samples collected in 2010–2012; 23 captive blood samples were separately identified in the study.

gaps: The short mitochondrial markers and regional samples do not establish a complete species phylogeny or genome-wide population history.

claims.text: The study collected wild fecal samples at 15 named locations in Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu in the Western Ghats. The sampling map documents this study's sites and is not a complete current range inventory.
claims.textZh: 该研究在西高止山脉的卡纳塔克邦、喀拉拉邦和泰米尔纳德邦 15 个具名地点采集了野生个体粪便样本。采样图记录的是本研究的地点，并非当前完整分布区名录。
claims.locator: Methods, “Study area”; Figure 1 and its caption; “Sample collection”.
claims.placeTimeScope: Western Ghats study localities in three Indian states; wild samples were collected during 2010–2012.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild-origin fecal samples; captive blood samples are separately described and are not treated as range records.

gaps: Study localities do not establish complete current occupancy or a full distribution boundary.
Fossil occurrence and the broader geological record were not reviewed; fossil calibrations in a molecular model are not a fossil inventory.

claims.text: Within the sampled Anamalai hills, HVR-I diversity was lower in eight forest fragments than in the adjacent continuous Nelliyampathy population. The comparison is based on mitochondrial markers from these sites and does not itself estimate current population viability or a formal conservation category.
claims.textZh: 在受采样的阿纳马莱丘陵地区，八个森林碎片中的 HVR-I 多样性低于邻近连续分布的内利亚姆帕蒂种群。该比较基于这些地点的线粒体标记，不能据此估算当前种群存续能力或正式保育等级。
claims.locator: Results, “Genetic diversity in the fragmented population of Anamalai hills”; Table 3; Discussion, “Effect of fragmentation on genetic diversity of lion-tailed macaques in Anamalai hills”.
claims.placeTimeScope: Eight Anamalai forest fragments compared with the continuous Nelliyampathy population in the Western Ghats; samples collected in 2010–2012.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild-origin fecal samples from free-ranging troops.

gaps: This local genetic comparison is not a current species-wide conservation assessment, abundance trend, or viability analysis.

reasons: Only regional mitochondrial evidence from one primary study was assessed; morphology, life history, and ecology remain not-assessed, while evolution, distribution, and conservation are partial.
No systematic literature search or independent expert review has been completed.

sources.title: Kiffner et al. (2022), Road-based line distance surveys overestimate densities of olive baboons
sources.version: PLOS ONE 17(2): e0263314; version of record published 2022-02-02
sources.locator: Abstract; Methods; Results and Discussion; Figure 2 and Tables 1–3.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the article copyright notice.
sources.scope: Primary field study comparing road-based line distance sampling with sleeping-site counts for wild olive baboons at Lake Manyara National Park, Tanzania, using monitoring from 2011–2019. Claims are paraphrased; figures and data files are not reused.
sources.rightsHolder: Christian Kiffner, Filipa M. D. Paciência, Grace Henrich, Rehema Kaitila, Idrissa S. Chuma, Pay Mbaryo, Sascha Knauf, John Kioko, Dietmar Zinner and coauthors as named in the article copyright notice.
sources.licenseAppliesTo: Article text under the stated CC BY 4.0 license; separately credited third-party material is excluded.
sources.attribution: Kiffner C, Paciência FMD, Henrich G, et al. (2022). Road-based line distance surveys overestimate densities of olive baboons. PLoS ONE 17(2):e0263314. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0263314. Claims are paraphrased.

gaps: The selected population-monitoring study does not assess anatomical morphology.
No life-cycle, reproductive, growth, survival, or longevity evidence was assessed.

claims.text: At Lake Manyara National Park, Tanzania, road-transect distance sampling from 2011–2019 produced an estimate more than three times the upper-limit abundance estimated from sleeping-site counts and average group size. The authors note that baboons' use of roads may explain the bias; this is a site- and method-specific result, not a species-wide density estimate.
claims.textZh: 在坦桑尼亚曼雅拉湖国家公园，2011 至 2019 年的道路样线距离抽样所得估计值，超过按夜宿地点数量和平均群体大小估算的数量上限三倍。作者指出，狒狒使用道路可能解释这种偏差；这是特定地点和方法的结果，不是物种层面的密度估计。
claims.locator: Abstract; Results and Discussion; Figure 2 and Tables 1–3.
claims.placeTimeScope: Lake Manyara National Park, Tanzania; road transects and sleeping-site comparison using surveys from 2011–2019.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild olive baboons in one protected area.

gaps: One protected-area monitoring study does not establish species-wide abundance, range-wide ecology, or a global population trend.
The monitoring study does not assess evolutionary history.
A single study site does not provide a geographic range inventory.
The selected study does not review the fossil record.
The site-level monitoring analysis does not constitute a current species-wide conservation assessment or formal risk category.

reasons: Only one site-specific population-monitoring study was assessed; six facets remain not-assessed and ecology is partial.
No systematic literature search or independent expert review has been completed.
